build.server: listing.controller setProductCoverPhotos (the row is held from the read to the write; only the cover_images key and the cover picture are written — jsonb_set; a record stored as text or missing is written whole with the row held, as before), brand.controller updateProduct (when a stock or sizes are sent, the read of the sizes and the write of the own number are one held step; with neither sent — Hide, Show, a new price — the same statements as before, no hold)
build.survey: every write of a product's colours-and-sizes record or its own number in backend/src was read (05-impact.md has the table). Two places wrote without holding the row: both fixed here. Left and named: the legacy flat product page sending its whole typed copy through the older save (fashion brands are redirected away from that page).
build.backend_new_suite: backend/tests/cover-photo-keeps-stock.test.js 8/8 (real API, real database). The moment is made by running a real order's stock movement (stock.service.moveProducts) on its own connection, leaving it open, sending the save, seeing it wait for the row in pg_stat_activity, then committing. Checks: a sale during a photo save stays sold; a cancelled order's piece during a photo save stays back; behaviour kept (photos added after the ones there, 6 at most, the first is the cover, nothing else in the record moves); the two refusals; a record stored as text; a product with no record; a sale during the older save with a stock; the older save with no stock sent.
build.red_first: run on the code as it was, three of those checks failed exactly as the fault describes: M back to 3 (expected 2); L back to 4 (expected 6); own number 7 with sizes adding to 6. (A fourth failure was the test's own wrong assumption that a new product has no photo list — corrected in the test, not in the code.)
